replication.target_description: Study 1: high- versus low-power posing, self-reported feelings of power, two-tailed t test, published p. 654.

n.exclusions: Five participants lack feelings-of-power information; three questionnaires were not saved correctly.
n.quote: Of the final ... sample of 200, 98 were women and 102 men. ... We did not have information on feelings of power for 5 par- ... ticipants. Three of these cases were the result of questionnaires ... not being saved correctly after laboratory maintenance.

reported_success.quote: We did ... find that power posing affected self-reported feelings of ... power; however, this did not yield behavioral effects.

notes: Identity independently checked: supplied text is the complete four-page published Commentary, Assessing the Robustness of Power Posing: No Effect on Hormones and Risk Tolerance in a Large Sample of Men and Women, by Eva Ranehill, Anna Dreber, Magnus Johannesson, Susanne Leiberg, Sunhae Sul, and Roberto A.
